MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 5, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR YOO at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Yoo, Medawar,  Olson,  Repp-Loadsman,  Romanelli,
  Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Nicklas

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

Director Naughton presented CHAIR YOO with a plaque and thanked him for his leadership and
continued service on the Planning Commission.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR is the Planning Commission Chair and COMMISSIONER OLSON is
Planning Commission Vice Chair.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JANUARY 8, 2024

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE CORRECTED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 8, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

NONE

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE

9.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386; LOCATION: 39 EMPTY SADDLE ROAD;
  APPLICANT: MICHAEL HASEGAWA ON BEHALF OF VERIZON WIRELESS;
  Application Withdrawal.

No discussion or comments on this item.

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE - COMMERCIAL DISTRICT

Director Naughton provided a presentation which included an overview of the actions of the
Planning Commission since adoption of the General Plan in 2022. A summary of the work
Planning Commission has done was presented to the City Council at its meeting on January 23,
2024. She provided a brief overview of the Form-Based and Euclidean code.

Director Naughton stated that the goal of producing a hybrid code is to make the code easier to

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 5, 2024
  1
 understand for those who may not be versed in the technical details of land use and providing
visuals and objective standards for those who are proposing projects in the commercial district.
Examples from other cities were provided.

Director Naughton provided an overview and examples of the various approaches in crafting
objective standards and zoning codes.

  •  True/False Statement – Statements of what the city would like to see along with clarifying
  language and/or an illustration.
  •  Counts and Measurement – Numeric values. These are already found in the city’s existing
  code. Examples include maximum building height or number of stories; ground floor height
  and upper story setbacks; public right-of-way widths.
  •  Ratios and Calculations – These are also already found in the city’s existing code.
  Examples include calculations for outdoor open space and common open space; ratio for
  parking/unit(s).

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there is a suggestion for a minimum of 10’ and the
projection for side and front yard setbacks are 5’ then yard space could not be counted towards
common open space. Director Naughton stated that this is correct and could be somewhat
different if the proposal is solely for residential.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if a porch can encroach into a 5’ front yard setback.
Director Naughton stated that it should be independent and setback to create the transition from
a public and private realm.

Director Naughton stated that the score card approach mentioned at the last meeting is more
appropriate for landscaping projects and instead suggested the list approach.

  •  List – allows more flexibility with discretionary aspects of a project. For example, if two or
  three are selected from a list of four or five, then the intent of the regulation would be met.

In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that there was
discussion at the General Plan Advisory Committee meetings about vacating Bart Earl Way, but
this was not supported by the City Council, and this was not included in the General Plan.
However, included is a focus on narrowing Silver Spur and improvement and landscaping of the
area between Bart Earl Way and Silver Spur as an option to be improved into a promenade.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the government code states that no personal or
subjective judgment can be used and asked what discretion the commission will have when these
objective design standards are implemented. Director Naughton stated that a lot of these
standards will apply to residential or mixed-use development and that the city agreed in the
Housing Element to remove the CUP requirement for these developments in the commercial
district. The CUP requirement will still be retained for the uses in commercial and mixed-use
development. Projects will still be subject to CEQA.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN clarified that there may be limitations on the commission’s
discretion on the design of a project. She suggested that if the city wants to encourage mixed-use
development and most developers are only proposing residential, then there should be an
incentive to motivate developers to design mixed-use projects.

COMMISSIONER REPP LOADSMAN inquired about applications that are submitted prior to the
adoption of the updated zoning code. Director Naughton stated that there was a bill passed that
states that if the city has a zoning code inconsistent with the General Plan then the city has 180
days to adopt a code that is consistent. If this does not occur, then the city must process the
application if it is consistent with the city’s General Plan. Director Naughton stated that there is
currently one application in process.

Director Naughton stated that at the next meeting staff will provide recent studies on the changing
landscape of retail. Staff will also provide a proposal for requiring or incentivizing mixed-use
developments.

COMMISSION REPP LOADSMAN asked for the timeframe within the 180 days for the current
application.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that the
initial efforts for the zoning code updates have been the commercial district since this had the
most changes. She provided an overview of what is coming up for the zoning code update at
future meetings.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 5, 2024
  2
 Director Naughton provided a brief overview of the changes in the commercial district, which
include:
  • Create a new Mixed-Use Overlay Zone.
  • Increase the base density from 22du/acre to 30du/acre.
  • Increase of the maximum building height to accommodate increased density.
  • Updated the parking requirements.
  • Modernize the list of uses.
  • Resolve discrepancies with allowable uses in the Commercial General and Commercial
  Limited Districts.
  • Encourage uses supported by the Vision Plan of the General Plan 2040.

Director Naughton stated that staff will provide a draft of the changes at the next Planning
Commission meeting in March.

10.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

NONE

11.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A.  COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

The commissioners agreed to the following committee assignments for 2024:

  •  Environmental Advisory Committee – Commissioner Repp-Loadsman
  •  Equestrian Committee – Commissioner Romanelli
  •  Traffic and Safety Committee – Vice Chair Olson

B.  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE 2024

No questions or comments

C.  PLANNING COMMISSION ATTENDANCE AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS - 2024
  SCHEDULE

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN, Director Naughton asked
that the commissioners email staff with any issues with the schedule.

Director Naughton stated that on January 23, 2024, the City Council held a first-look meeting for
a proposal to develop the property at 655-815 Deep Valley Drive and 924-950 Indian Peak Road.
The staff report and plans can be found on the city’s website. No discussion can be held since
this is not an agendized item. A brief summary of the project was provided.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that the
City Council provided feedback and there was concern about the amount of non-residential. The
direction from the City Council was to provide more non-residential and for the developer to work
with the existing tenants and try to provide accommodation. There was also concern that the
design does not fit in with the commercial district.

Director Naughton stated that the minutes will provide more detail and can be found on the city’s
website in the coming week.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if an application is submitted under SB330, would
this be the type of application that would vest them in the current ordinance. Director Naughton
stated yes.

12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, DECEMBER 12, 2023

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 12A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on March 4, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.in the City
